kaps_punt: Onderwerp 4 - Waardeer en nadenke, Kwartaal 2. Die uitdrukkingskwaliteite van slaginstrumente in ŉ Afrika-musiekstuk. Klassifiseer verskeie instrumente as deel van ŉ familie of groep in terme van voorkoms, benoeming, hoe die klank voortgebring word en die toonhoogte klassifikasie (hoog-laag). Eie en ander se optredes en prosesse deur die gebruik van eenvoudige skeppende kunsterminologie.

items.bewering: kaps_punt: "Die uitdrukkingskwaliteite van slaginstrumente in ŉ Afrika-musiekstuk."
items.bron: Afrikaans KABV Lewensvaardighede Graad 4-6, Graad 4 Kwartaal 2, Onderwerp 4 'Waardeer en nadenke', PDF bl. 41: "Die uitdrukkingskwaliteite van slaginstrumente in 'n Afrika-musiekstuk. Klassifiseer verskeie instrumente as deel van 'n familie of groep in terme van voorkoms, benoeming, hoe die klank voortgebring word en die toonhoogte klassifikasie (hoog-laag)." I did not read this page myself. The pipeline owner read it and the coordinator relayed it on 22 Sep 2026, after I failed to open the Afrikaans KABV online (the DBE file returned only its cover). For the record, the English CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6 (Gr 4 Term 2 Topic 4, printed p. 34) says 'melodic musical instruments' instead (https://www.education.gov.za/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=OX12620gNnw%3D&tabid=572&portalid=0&mid=1568). That is a difference between the two language versions of CAPS and not a fault in this lesson, which follows the Afrikaans version it is written against.

items.bron: Blacking/ERA: 'Drums are always played by women and girls, except in possession dances, when men may play them', and the thungwa is 'the same shape as, but smaller than, ngoma'. The set is one ngoma, one thungwa and 2 or 3 murumba (http://www.era.anthropology.ac.uk/Era_Resources/Era/VendaGirls/VendaMusic/Mu_I_Text2.html). Given that exception, 'gewoonlik' is the correct careful wording.

items.bewering: Die grootste en diepste trom wat die VhaVenda gebruik, met beesvel oor uitgeholde hout.
items.bron: Blacking/ERA, 'Bass drum (ngoma)': the ngoma is the bass drum of the ngomani set, with the murumba as alto and the thungwa as tenor drums, and the thungwa is the same shape but smaller (http://era.anthropology.ac.uk/Era_Resources/Era/VendaGirls/Milayo/M_Drum.html; http://www.era.anthropology.ac.uk/Era_Resources/Era/VendaGirls/VendaMusic/Mu_I_Text2.html). The murumba is held between the thighs, so it is smaller. 'Diepste' matches the bass role. The ox-hide and hollowed wood are as in the ngoma block.

items.bron: Hartenberger WMIC, 'Zulu Cocoon Ankle Rattles': Argema mimosae cocoons 'filled with sand or small stones and then sewn onto ropes', 'wrapped around the ankle', used by the Zulu of South Africa in traditional dancing (https://wmic.net/zulu-cocoon-ankle-rattles/). Other southern African leg rattles (e.g. Tswana matlhowa) are also made from dried cocoons. Some are filled with stones or seeds rather than sand, but 'vol sand' is documented and true of real examples.

items.bewering: Neem nou twee leë blikke wat presies dieselfde lyk. Sit sade in die een en maak riwwe in die ander se sy. Die een word nou geskud en die ander word geskraap. Hoe die klank gemaak word, bepaal die familie en nie hoe iets lyk nie.
items.bron: Mapping checked against Hornbostel-Sachs, which classifies instruments by how the sound is made. A tin with seeds is a vessel rattle (112.13, shaken), and a tin with ridges scraped by a stick is a scraped vessel (112.2), so two identical-looking objects land in different groups. The thought experiment maps correctly. It does not contradict the 'four questions' in the first block, because appearance stays a sorting question and is only denied as what fixes the family. A learner reasoning further (for example, 'a tin with seeds that I scrape') would still reach the right answer, since the rule follows the action. The heading says 'Die klank' where the body says 'Hoe die klank gemaak word'. The body text states the correct rule.

items.blok: Wat elke instrument aan die stuk doen
items.bron: This is a listening instruction, and its only implied claim is that African ensemble pieces usually have a steady timekeeping part. Tracey & Gumboreshumba (African Music, Rhodes/ILAM) call the thungwa drum 'the time-keeper' in tshikona. Wikipedia, Hosho (instrument) and Shona music describe the hosho's steady timekeeping role in mbira music. The sentences are hedged ('Dalk') and set a task rather than asserting what every piece contains.

DBE CAPS Gr 4 Term 2 Topic 4: 'Own and other's performances and processes using simple creative arts terminology'. 'Eerste' here refers to order within the group's own performance and is not a superlative claim.

items.bron: Hornbostel-Sachs, the standard organological classification, groups instruments by how the sound is produced (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hornbostel%E2%80%93Sachs). Read alone, the entry also fits orchestral families (strings, woodwind, brass, percussion), which are likewise defined by how the sound is made, so it does not mislead outside this lesson.

opsomming: All 31 claims are confirmed, including the ngoma superlative and the two-tins comparison, and the one open question closed when the pipeline owner confirmed that the Afrikaans CAPS names percussion instruments, although the English CAPS says melodic instruments for this bullet.
